svg.title: A stable tensor-square isomorphism would split the prime free factor
svg.desc: Assume a normal unital isomorphism from S(N) to S(N tensor N), with N equal to the countably generated free group factor. The image p of the unit matrix corner has finite positive trace t by Lemma 5J.2. Construct q in S(N) with the same trace and compare p with q tensor 1. The resulting corner is K tensor N, with K diffuse and finite, so N would split into two infinite-dimensional factors. Ozawa's primeness theorem excludes this. For the one-sided pair in equation 5F.5, M1 and P1 have type S(N) while Q1 has type S(N tensor N).

g.text: Stable tensor squares
N = L(F∞), with countably many generators

Φ : S(N) ≅ S(N ⊗ N)
Normal and unital; no trace scale is specified.
Image of the unit matrix corner
p = Φ(E₀₀ ⊗ 1), p R p ≅ N
Lemma 5J.2 proves 0 < T(p) = t < ∞.
R = S(N ⊗ N), with its canonical product trace
Place the same trace in the first factor
q = ∑ⱼ₌₀ᵏ⁻¹ Eⱼⱼ ⊗ 1 + Eₖₖ ⊗ rₛ
τ_N(rₛ) = s, T_N(q) = t
An empty sum and a zero arc projection are allowed.
Finite-trace comparison in R
v* v = p, v v* = q ⊗ 1
N ≅ (q S(N) q) ⊗ N
K = q S(N) q is a diffuse finite factor.
Contradiction to primeness
Both K and N are infinite dimensional.
Theorem 5J.3 excludes the assumed Φ.
Analytic input: Ozawa, Theorem 1 and Proposition 2
Application to the actual pair (5F.5)
M₁ ≅ P₁ ≅ S(N)
Q₁ ≅ S(N ⊗ N)
Q₁ is not isomorphic to M₁.
No Hilbert-space unitary exchanges P₁ and Q₁.
Corollary 5J.4 concerns this specified one-sided pair.
S(P) = B(ℓ²ℕ) ⊗ P · all tensor products are spatial
